title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو حفظه الله يخطب بالدوحة عن تغيير المنكر
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew, May God Preserve Him, Preaches in Doha on Changing Wrong
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن ولد الددو خطبة الجمعة اليوم 12 صفر 1433هـ الموافق: 06/01/2012 بجامع الإمام محمد بن عبد الوهاب في العاصمة القطرية الدوحة وسط حضور عشرات الآلاف من المصلين في الجامع الذي يعتبر أكبر جامع في دولة قطر.

وقد تحدث الشيخ في خطبته عن تغيير المنكر ووجوب تغييره على من شهده، مذكرا بمراتب المناكر وضوابط تغييرها، مؤكدا أن المنكر يعظم كلما تعاظمت آثاره وزاد انتشاره، وهو ما يدعو للأخذ على يد الظالم قبل أن يغرق بظلمه سفينة الحياة وتعم العقوبة الجميع ولا تفرق بين المشاركين في الظلم والساكتين عليه.

تأتي خطبة الشيخ في الجامع الذي تم تدشينه مؤخرا خلال زيارة يقوم بها الشيخ لدولة قطر، حيث يقوم الشيخ بالعديد من الأنشطة العلمية الهامة.
body_en:
His Eminence the learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew delivered the Friday sermon today, 12 Safar 1433 AH, corresponding to 06/01/2012, at the Mosque of Imam Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab in the Qatari capital, Doha, amid an attendance of tens of thousands of worshippers at the mosque, which is regarded as the largest mosque in the State of Qatar.

In his sermon the Sheikh spoke of changing wrong, and of the obligation (wujūb) of changing it that falls upon whoever witnesses it, recalling the degrees of wrongs and the constraints governing the changing of them, and affirming that a wrong grows greater as its effects grow greater and its spread increases — which is what calls for taking hold of the oppressor's hand, before he sinks with his injustice the ship of life, and the punishment becomes general to all and does not distinguish between those who took part in the injustice and those who kept silent about it.

The Sheikh's sermon comes at the mosque recently inaugurated, during a visit the Sheikh is making to the State of Qatar, in which he is undertaking numerous important scholarly activities.

flags.context: the single sentence that reports the sermon's content
options: display with a prominent caveat that the constraints are not in the record
display as a statement of his position
flags.note: critical_for_display, and in a particularly clean form. The record reports the obligation of changing wrong, says that the Sheikh went through the degrees of wrongs and the constraints governing their change, and then gives not one of those constraints. In this area of the law the constraints are the whole of the matter: the classical discussion turns on who may act, by what means, against whom, and when acting would cause greater harm than it removes. What survives in English is the obligation with the limits stripped off, followed by a sentence about taking hold of the oppressor's hand. That is precisely the shape the style guide's section 10 warns about, and the record must not be rendered as a fatwa.

options: that it is obligatory (wājib) to change it
flags.note: وجوب is the abstract noun of wājib and takes the fixed mapping of style guide section 3: 'obligation', not 'duty', which would blur it towards the merely moral. The record does not say whether the obligation reported is individual (farḍ ʿayn) or communal (farḍ kifāyah), and that distinction is decisive for what it asks of a reader; 'upon whoever witnesses it' points towards the individual, but the record does not say so and the translator must not settle it.

flags.arabic: قبل أن يغرق بظلمه سفينة الحياة وتعم العقوبة الجميع
flags.context: the image used in the sermon
options: render the image as it stands, with no gloss
add a note identifying the allusion
flags.note: The image alludes to the well-known prophetic parable of those who draw lots for places on a ship and of the man below deck who would bore a hole in the hull — the parable of enjoining right and forbidding wrong. The record does not present it as a quotation, gives no collection and no grading, and does not name the parable. The English carries the image and adds nothing; the allusion is recorded here instead. Note that سفينة الحياة, 'the ship of life', is the reporter's variation on the image, not the wording of the report.

flags.context: what the growing spread of a wrong calls for
options: taking hold of the oppressor's hand
staying the hand of the wrongdoer
flags.note: A fixed Arabic idiom drawn from the hadith of enjoining right, and already rendered 'take hold of the oppressor's hand' in record 754 of this corpus; the same rendering is used here for consistency. The literal image is kept because the paraphrase 'restraining' would not show the reader that a known formula is being used.

translator_notes: A very short news report of a Friday sermon. Nothing is quoted; the whole of the sermon's content is one reported sentence. The sermon itself is not in the corpus, and this record carries no link to a recording.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body's dates agree with each other and with the timestamp: 12 Safar 1433 was Friday 6 January 2012.

المنكر is rendered 'wrong' throughout, following the glossary's al-nahy ʿan al-munkar, 'forbidding wrong'. مناكر in the plural is 'wrongs'. 'Evil' and 'vice' are avoided: both are stronger in English and shift the term from the legal register to the moral one.
The ruling word here attaches to an act and takes the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3; the kalām exemption of section 8 is not engaged.

This record and 779, six days apart, report two lectures on closely related subjects and read very differently in English: 779 states four rulings and 780 states one and withholds its conditions. Both should be weighed together by whoever decides what is displayed.
